verdicts.quote: the owner defines the reminder schedule as an ordered list of integer day offsets from an invoice's due date (0 = due date, positive = days after, negative = days before)
If at that moment the invoice has no outstanding balance, or is void, written off, or paused, nothing is sent ... A partial payment reduces the balance that is shown and does not stop reminders
verdicts.missing: Payment plans are never mentioned, and a disputed invoice stops only if the owner pauses it by hand (R-9). The builder still has to decide whether either one stops the sequence automatically.

verdicts.quote: A balance of 100.00 on an invoice of 250.00 (partial payment) shows `100.00 USD`, never 250.00.
Out of scope: ... customer opt-out or unsubscribe handling beyond R-9's owner-side pause.
verdicts.missing: Whether a do-not-contact or unsubscribed flag the host already holds on a customer is honoured, and whether billing notices are exempt from a marketing opt-out.

verdicts.quote: before any email is attempted the job atomically claims `(invoice, step offset)` in the ledger. Only the claim winner sends ... re-running the job the same day, two overlapping runs, and a crash between claim and recording are all covered
the job re-reads the invoice immediately before each send ... the check is per send, not per run, so a payment recorded between the scan and the send stops that send.
it is retried on each following daily run while it remains the latest eligible step ... For the last step the retry bound is open (G-3)
verdicts.missing: The retry bound for the last step is open (G-3). Escalating repeated failures to a person, by notification or alert, is left open (G-6); failures are only visible in the history.

verdicts.quote: the mail provider's send quota and rate ... are unknown, so no numeric bound is stated ... if a run stops early at any runtime or provider limit, every unprocessed invoice's due steps stay unrecorded
verdicts.missing: How sends are paced to stay within the provider's rate limit. The spec only covers a run that has already stopped at a limit.

verdicts.quote: steps scheduled before `effective_from` are never sent; a newly saved schedule does not mass-mail existing overdue invoices unless the owner sets `effective_from` back (A-3, a deliberate safeguard against an outward burst).
the day boundary is local midnight in the business timezone, not UTC.
verdicts.missing: Whether to use the customer's local time, and which sending hours apply: the time of day is left as a deployment setting (A-9). Weekends and holidays are only excluded in the sense that business-day and holiday calendars are out of scope (R-1).

verdicts.quote: Out of scope: multi-currency conversion (amounts are shown in the invoice's own currency, unconverted)
a missing or syntactically invalid recipient address means no send; the step is recorded `skipped_no_recipient` with no retry for that step (a later step uses the then-current address).
each reminder is one email to the invoice's billing contact address ... Boundaries: one invoice per email; one recipient address; no CC or BCC to the owner.
verdicts.missing: Which contact gets the email when a customer has more than one billing contact.

verdicts.quote: for any invoice the owner can see each ledger row: step offset, scheduled date, state ... attempt count, last-attempt timestamp, the mail provider's accepted-message identifier when present.

It states: business name, invoice number, outstanding balance with currency, due date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) ... If the host exposes a payment link for the invoice it is included, otherwise the message omits it.
verdicts.missing: Whether the payment link expires, and how an expired link is handled.

verdicts.quote: Only the owner role can read history, change the schedule, or pause an invoice.
Rollback: disabling the feature is clearing the schedule (R-1), which stops all sends from the next run
verdicts.missing: A preview or dry run. Manual resend is excluded (R-8, 'no edit or manual resend') and so is customer-level pause (R-9), so there is no per-customer off switch.

verdicts.quote: `unknown` and `failed` rows are distinguishable at a glance and can be listed across invoices.
verdicts.missing: A way to see which reminders the system will send next.

verdicts.quote: strictly increasing (so at most one step per invoice per calendar day, which is the only per-day volume bound this feature introduces)
verdicts.missing: An overall cap on sending volume, which is unresolved (NFR-4, G-5), and a limit on how late a missed step may still go out.

verdicts.quote: Invoice records (balance, status, due date, contact) | host invoicing system (G-1) | observed only | never written by this feature; reads always fresh
